title: Get orders-api through Black Friday

ticket.subject: orders-api: public route and autoscaling before Black Friday
body: orders-api runs in the `shop` namespace of our AKS cluster with two replicas (the manifests are in `k8s/`).
Two things must be ready before Friday:
- **The public route.** The storefront calls `http://shop.contoso.test/api/orders`. Sam started
`k8s/ingress.yaml` but never applied it: the cluster's ingress controller is ingress-nginx (class `nginx`)
and every path under `/api` must reach the `orders-api` Service.
- **Autoscaling.** Last year's Black Friday load is recorded; `lab load replay` plays it against the cluster.
Add a HorizontalPodAutoscaler (`autoscaling/v2`) on CPU utilization, target **70 %**, between **2** and
**10** replicas. From the load test, each pod needs `cpu: 250m` and `memory: 256Mi` requested and must
never use more than `cpu: 600m` and `memory: 512Mi` (limits). During the replay no minute may have the
pods overloaded (every pod at its CPU limit), and once the rush is over we go back to 2 replicas.
Show me the replay output when you're done. Keep everything in the `shop` namespace.
This is the lab's simulated cluster: nothing is deployed.

hints: Everything lives in the `shop` namespace: `kubectl get all -n shop`, `kubectl get ingress -n shop`. Without `-n shop`, kubectl looks in `default`.
`kubectl apply -f k8s/` reports an invalid object and applies the others. An Ingress path needs a `pathType`: `Prefix` matches `/api` and everything under it, `Exact` only `/api` itself.
An Ingress is ignored when no controller claims its class: `kubectl get ingressclass` lists them; set `spec.ingressClassName`.

The Ingress backend names a port of the Service (`port: 80`, or its name `http`), not the container's port. `kubectl describe ingress orders-api -n shop` shows each backend and its endpoints; `curl -v` explains a 404 or 503.
The HPA computes utilization as usage over the pod's CPU request: without `resources.requests.cpu` it cannot scale (`kubectl describe hpa -n shop` says why).

`lab load replay` prints the replicas minute by minute: if the pods are overloaded at the peak, the maximum is too low or the pods too small; the scale-down waits 5 minutes (the default stabilization window).
